decision: MIXED — partial support for discriminating operating point under overlap. The frozen decision_rule requires BOTH: (1) calibrated threshold increases with overlap — TRUE (0.20→0.25 at 100% overlap); (2) FP > 0 at threshold 0.20 for overlap >=25% — FALSE (FP=0.0 at 25% and 50%, nonzero only at 75%=0.0958 and 100%=0.35). The threshold does increase but only at extreme (full) overlap, not gradually as hypothesized. FP binding emerges only at 75%+ overlap, not at the hypothesized >=25%. However, the audit identifies that the overlap operationalization was materially flawed: the code shift (overlap_pct/100*0.09) produces 0% actual distributional overlap at the 25% and 50% conditions, so FP=0 at those conditions is an artifact of insufficient shift, not evidence against discrimination. The threshold calibration grid is coarse discrete [0.20,0.25,...0.80] — the true optimum between 0.20 and 0.25 was not probed. Orthogonality marginal failure at 75% overlap (CI upper 0.1549 > 0.15) is flagged but may be sample-size artifact at n=480. Audit status REVISE, not PASS. No PRODUCT_CORE promotion authorized. C-FRESHNESS remains EXPERIMENTAL.

claim_updates.reason: MIXED outcome: threshold increases at 100% overlap only (not gradual as hypothesized), FP binding at 75%+ not >=25%. Audit REVISE: overlap operationalization flawed (code shift 0.09*overlap_pct/100 produces 0% actual overlap at 25%/50%), threshold grid coarse discrete [0.20,0.25,...], orthogonality marginal failure at 75% (CI upper 0.1549 > 0.15, possible sample-size artifact). Claim ceiling narrowed: calibrated threshold 0.20 survives label shift up to 75% (actual overlap ~8%, FP=0.0958 < 0.10) on localhost mock only. FP constraint becomes binding only at 75% overlap (actual overlap ~8%, FP=0.0958) and 100% overlap (actual overlap ~33%, FP=0.35 forces threshold to 0.25). Orthogonality TOST delta=0.15 holds at 4/5 overlap conditions (r -0.004 to 0.036), marginal failure at 75% (r=0.066 CI upper 0.1549). Discrimination 0.8333 and 4/4 noise types remain effective. No evidence for production OAuth/OIDC, CDN, network RTT, DB sessions, or non-uniform production refresh distributions. Do NOT promote to PRODUCT_CORE or VALIDATED.

product_action: No product promotion authorized. C-FRESHNESS remains EXPERIMENTAL on localhost mock only. The overlap experiment reveals the freshness guard is robust to moderate noise-refresh overlap (0-75% label overlap with actual overlap ~8%) but breaks down at full overlap (100% label shift, 33% actual overlap, FP=0.35). Two open questions block PRODUCT_CORE: (1) does discrimination hold under corrected overlap design with genuine 25%/50% distributional overlap, and (2) does orthogonality survive on production substrate with real OAuth/OIDC, CDN, network RTT, DB-backed sessions. The first requires a redesigned experiment (Gaussian overlap or symmetric failure-distribution shift); the second requires runtime lane production-like substrate.
next_question: Can the freshness guard discriminating operating point be measured under genuine overlap (25%/50%/75% distributional area) using Gaussian or symmetric-overlap noise/refresh distributions on localhost mock — and does the calibrated threshold increase gradually (not just at 100% overlap) when the overlap is real rather than an artifact of uniform-shift boundary behavior?
reason: The experiment partially resolves the parent's threshold tautology: FP constraint becomes binding at 75% overlap (FP=0.0958) and the threshold shifts to 0.25 at 100% overlap (FP=0.35), demonstrating that discrimination exists under extreme overlap. However, the overlap design is materially flawed — the uniform-shift implementation produces 0% actual distributional overlap at 25% and 50% label-overlap conditions, so FP=0 at those conditions is a design artifact not evidence against discrimination. The coarse threshold grid [0.20,0.25,...0.80] cannot locate the true optimum between 0.20 and 0.25. The marginal orthogonality failure at 75% (CI upper 0.1549 vs delta 0.15) requires investigation at n>=800. Parent's core finding (C-FRESHNESS orthogonality at delta=0.15 on localhost stochastic mock, 6 independent confirmations) is not superseded by this experiment. The mock-only ceiling persists — no production OAuth/OIDC, CDN, network RTT, or DB-backed sessions tested.
